deep.reconstruction:
This page is a laboratory log from the Göttingen magnetometer work of the 1830s. It is instrument adjustment, not mathematics. There are three blocks.

(1) Mirror-collimation check, continued from the previous page.
- On the previous page the correction screw at the mirror was calibrated. One thread = 3.7 mm / 9 1/8 threads ≈ 0.405 mm, acting on a radius of 56 mm. One turn therefore rotates the mirror by 0.405/56 rad = 0.0072321 rad ≈ 1491.7'' = 24'52'', which was said to equal 55.5 scale divisions.
- Reversal readings (West/East) gave optical-axis positions whose half-difference measures the error of the mirror normal relative to the magnetic axis. The sequence was:
  - 309.52 / 209.75: half-difference 49.885 div.
  - After 3/4 turn: 269.5 / 250.9, half-difference 9.3. The change of 40.6 div matches the predicted 0.75 × 55.5 = 41.6.
  - After 1/6 turn: 257.2 / 253.9, half-difference 1.65. The change of 7.65 div compares with the predicted 9.25.
- On this page, after a further correction along the short diameter and a touch-up along the long diameter (determined with the latter horizontal), the readings are West 261.3, East 267.2.
- Mean = 264.25. Index error = ±(267.2 − 261.3)/2 = ±2.95 divisions, written as ±80.5''. This implies a scale value of 80.5/2.95 ≈ 27.29'' per division.

(2) 27 May: re-stroking the large magnet.
- The (double) deflection was 78.325.
- Needle A laid against end A of the horseshoe (sketch with ends A, B) gave a deflection of 60.1875.
- After stroking it gave 89.25. Ratio 89.25/60.1875 ≈ 1.483, i.e. about a 48% increase in magnetization as measured by deflection.

(3) 1 June: new suspension apparatus; height bookkeeping.
- Mirror height 819 mm; opening 54 mm.
- The scale was lowered 14 mm and now measures 423.4 mm, 'thus 4.6 mm too low'. The intended height is therefore 428.0 mm (my inference: 423.4 + 4.6). The scale was previously at 437.4 mm.
- Objective centre height 1190 mm. The new scale is now 443 mm high.
- My remark: for a vertical mirror with scale and objective at comparable distances, the symmetric height would be 2·819 − 1190 = 448 mm. The 443 is close to this, but the page does not state the rule used.
errors: Scale value inconsistency: 80.5''/2.95 = 27.29'' per division, whereas the previous page's calibration (1491.7'' = 55.5 div) gives 26.88''/div. With that value, 2.95 div ≈ 79.3'', not 80.5''. The likely cause is a different adopted scale constant, not necessarily an error.
The predicted effect of the 1/6 turn (9.25 div) versus the observed change (7.65 div) differs noticeably. This is plausibly due to screw backlash and is not commented on.
The target height of 428 mm for the scale is not obviously derived from the 819 and 1190 figures; the basis is unstated.

results.what: Determination of mirror-normal collimation error by reversal (West/East) readings and its correction via a calibrated screw
results.modern_name: Reversal method for collimation error; Poggendorff–Gauss mirror-and-scale reading

results.what: Re-magnetization of a horseshoe magnet by stroking, checked by deflection of a needle
Height adjustment of scale relative to mirror and telescope objective for the new suspension

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine experimental log of magnetometer adjustment and magnet re-stroking, well within known Gauss–Weber laboratory work. It contains no novel mathematics.

checkable.asserts: Implied scale value ≈ 27.29 arcsec per division
Symmetric reflection height for vertical mirror = 448 mm
